questions.key_step: Rewrite arcsin(y/r) as arctan(y/x), then differentiate twice.
questions.justification: Routine chain: simplification, one implicit derivative, second derivative with algebra; no new idea.

questions.key_step: Compare degrees to get a cubic, then match coefficients.
questions.justification: Degree comparison plus coefficient matching; both are familiar polynomial moves.

questions.key_step: Differentiate with respect to y to get 5y = sqrt(x^2-1) y'.
questions.justification: Hidden cosh substitution; the derivative chain is short and routine.

questions.key_step: Substitute x=1 in the identity and in its derivative to get f''=f'^2 and f'f''=8.
questions.justification: Functional-differential identity; the idea of differentiating the identity and substituting x=1 is not routine and a slip in the product rule gives a wrong answer.

questions.key_step: dz/dx = 1/sin x converts d/dx into sin x d/dz.
questions.justification: Standard change of variable; two chain-rule steps.

questions.key_step: Differentiate y = tan z twice and substitute.
questions.justification: Same technique as 5(a) but algebra needs care; routine.

questions.key_step: Put y' = tan(theta); get y'' = sec^3/R and x_yy = -cosec^3/R.
questions.justification: Needs inverse-function second derivative and radius of curvature; a student must find the angle substitution; real cube-root sign care.

questions.key_step: p(1)=0 from the bound, then the derivative as a limit gives |p'(1)|<=1.
questions.justification: Official JEE 2000 idea: squeeze plus first-principles derivative; short but not a routine move.

questions.key_step: e^{g(x)} = x + sqrt(1+x^2) cancels the denominator of f'(1/x).
questions.justification: One cancellation observed after a chain of routine derivatives.

questions.key_step: Check f, f' and f'' at the joining point x=0.
questions.justification: Several routine checks of continuity and differentiability at one point.

questions.key_step: Only column 1 contains x after column operations; sum of cofactors = k.
questions.justification: Determinant derivative plus cofactor identification; two linked ideas, expansion sign errors likely.

questions.key_step: 1^infinity form for x->0; factor out the dominant term for x->+-infinity.
questions.justification: Three limits of different types; the dominant-term factoring is standard but all three must be right.

questions.key_step: Divide P by (x-x1)^2 and apply L'Hospital twice.
questions.justification: Needs the idea of dividing a double root out and a limit to identify Q; unusual for students.

questions.key_step: P^4+P^2+1 = (P^2-P+1)(P^2+P+1) cancels the denominator.
questions.justification: One factorisation then a routine second derivative.

questions.key_step: Differentiate g(f(x)) = x three times at x=0.
questions.justification: Standard inverse-function derivative chain; precision needed but routine.

questions.key_step: With 8x-16=p^2 each radicand is a perfect square, leaving |p+4|+|p-4|.
questions.justification: Numerical answer; the nested-radical simplification and the modulus junction are not routine.

questions.key_step: sqrt(x^2-a^2) y' = 2 ln(...) + k; differentiate again.
questions.justification: Short routine derivative chain; k cancels.

questions.key_step: y = x ln(x/(a+bx)) gives xy'-y = ax/(a+bx).
questions.justification: Logarithmic differentiation twice; routine algebra.

questions.key_step: tan((x+b)/2a) = a ln y gives 2a^2 y'/y = 1 + a^2 ln^2 y.
questions.justification: Implicit differentiation twice; routine.

questions.key_step: Put alpha = 3y^2-1; everything reduces to a polynomial identity in alpha.
questions.justification: Long, precise algebra in an identity proof; a slip anywhere destroys the proof.

questions.key_step: (fg)' = f'g' with f = x^3 gives g'/g = 3/(3-x).
questions.justification: Separable DE from a verbal condition; routine once set up.

questions.key_step: The product f(x-3)g(x) is the constant 9.
questions.justification: One observation (or a short product rule).

questions.key_step: Limit equals lim 9x^2/((3-x)^3+9) = 0.
questions.justification: Direct limit after substitution.

questions.key_step: Factor 1-cos^3 x and recognise 1/f.
questions.justification: Short derivative simplification with a factoring step.

questions.key_step: g' >= 0 iff lambda >= f(x); range of f is (0,1/3].
questions.justification: Isolate the parameter and find the range of a simple function.
Four short items, each a one-step idea.
